what: Ally is an online bank with no branches. Its largest business is car loans, inherited from its days as General Motors' finance arm, funded by deposits gathered online at competitive rates.
customers: Car buyers financing through dealers, and savers who want a better deposit rate than a branch bank pays.
money: car loans and leases originated through dealers
vehicle service contracts and dealer insurance
moat: Relationships with thousands of car dealers built over a century, combined with a deposit base gathered without the cost of branches.
risks: Car loan losses rise when unemployment rises, and the borrower mix skews toward weaker credit
Deposit costs move up quickly with rates, squeezing the margin
Used car values set what a repossessed car recovers, and they have been falling
opportunities: Analysts see about 28% upside, with 18 covering the stock
Falling interest rates would widen the net interest margin, since deposit costs reprice faster than the loan book
watch: Net charge-off rates on car loans and the net interest margin.
